title: Kunzia Confederation
subtitle: Design Web

layers.label: Constitutional Layer
layers.description: The immutable core document. Additive-only. Recognizes natural rights. All unlisted powers default to cells. No international authority recognized.

items.label: Additive-only amendment
items.desc: 3/4 coordination body + 75% popular supermajority to add. Never subtractive.

notes.quote: Adding requires a 3/4 vote by some form of yet to be defined leadership and  a 75 percent popular vote if grassroots defined. This document can be added to but never taken away from.

items.explanation: Additive-only. 3/4 coordination body + 75% popular supermajority to amend. Never subtractive.

items.label: Natural rights recognized
items.desc: Rights recognized, not granted. Source-agnostic: deism, Christianity, secular reason.

notes.quote: I believe there is an objective natural law of rights that can be defended through deism, Christianity, or several other secular means as well

items.explanation: Recognized, not granted. Defensible through deism, Christianity, or secular reason equally. Source-agnostic.

items.label: NAP as default norm
items.desc: Non-Aggression Principle is the baseline behavioral standard. Voluntarism first.

notes.quote: The nonaggression principle is a good place to start I would say that I try to lead voluntarists first.

items.explanation: The baseline behavioral standard. Voluntarism first.

items.label: 10th/9th analog
items.desc: All unlisted powers default explicitly to cells. No implied federal authority.

notes.quote: I would say Switzerland and its loosely affiliated cantons with individual constitutions is pretty close. The 10th US amendment will apply in combination with the 9th but directly clearly pointed to the cells.

items.explanation: All unlisted powers default to cells. No implied central authority.

items.label: No international authority
items.desc: System sovereignty is absolute. International cooperation is transactional, not binding.
items.explanation: No international authority recognized. Cooperation is transactional, never binding. Cooperation with NATO and similar bodies only as needed for true global threats or worldwide economic crashes.

notes.quote: We won't recognize international authority, working with NATO etc. but only as needed to address true global threats or worldwide economy crashes etc.

items.label: Speech — radical, NAP-bounded
items.desc: Maximum freedom of speech. NAP is the only limit. Cells handle nuance.

notes.quote: Next would be a radical freedom of speech based on NAP. Rules for handling nuance are held by the cells.

items.explanation: Speech: radical, NAP-bounded. Cell nuance permitted.

items.label: Religion — NAP-tested
items.desc: Subsumed under speech. Voluntary practice protected. Governance application that mandates non-voluntary compliance = constitutional void.

notes.quote: Freedom of religion will wrap under speech but caveat issues like Islamism under NAP that have ANY rules that directly violate freedoms noted in cells without a method of voluntary following. It would effectively make shariah law for example a non-starter.

items.explanation: Religion: subsumed under speech, NAP-tested. Voluntary practice protected. A governance application that mandates non-voluntary compliance is constitutionally void (Shariah as governance: void. Shariah as personal practice: protected).

items.label: Arms — tiered
items.desc: Household issue baseline. Personal through Class III constitutional. Cell militia for heavy. WMD equally distributed.
items.explanation: Tiered: household-issue baseline, then personal and Class III arms (constitutional), then cell militias for heavy weapons. WMD are equally distributed across cells. Concealed carry and self-manufacture are constitutional up to Class III (automatic infantry weapons). Explosives, missiles and armor are reserved to cell militias, reachable by individuals only through difficult, restrictive processes. Making, buying and selling carry cell nuance.

notes.quote: Weapons will be issued per defined household for all cells. Conceal carry and self manufacture are core items up to class III which is automatic infantry weapons. Explosives, missiles, tanks, etc. are reserved for individual militias of cells, but can be accessed with difficult restrictive processes.

items.label: Travel — citizen floor
items.desc: Search/seizure protections apply everywhere. Cell-licensed nuance (driving, etc.).

notes.quote: Freedom of travel applies to a base set of elements like search and seizure everywhere, but cell constitutions can regulate nuance like licenses or training requirements for driving etc. There will be no DMV though, either it is private or small and localized to centers of authority within the cells.

items.explanation: Constitutional floor for citizens, with search and seizure protections everywhere. Cells license the details (driving and similar).

items.label: V+1 criminal standard
items.desc: Retributive proportionality plus one degree for violent crime. Massive deterrent architecture.
items.explanation: Punishment is proportional to the harm, plus one degree for violent crime. Owner's framing: robbing and beating someone to death would mean a slower beating to death. Applies to multi-factor battery, murder, rape and torture, not to fights or threats.

notes.quote: Core obvious rights would be eye for eye on violent crimes +1 , maybe call it V+1 , which means robbing and beating someone to death would mean a slower beating of that individual to death--massive deterrent against violent crimes that aren't just fights or threats etc. but multi fact battery, murder, rape, torture.

items.label: Execution — tiered delegation
items.desc: Victim (first right) → volunteer pool (random selection) → automated chamber. Randomized actuation, 3 fast methods, fire cleanup. No permanent executor class.

notes.quote: The execution of the sentence will be given to the victim when there is a clear one for choice. After that, there will be a body of volunteers willing to pool a random selection, and on the rare event that an entire cell is against volunteering at all, we will use technology as a failsafe. This whole system only matters if the victim and all others don't participate.

items.explanation: Victim has first right; then a randomly selected volunteer pool; then an automated chamber (randomized actuation, three fast methods, fire cleanup). No permanent executioner class.

items.label: National security body
items.desc: Transparently chartered. Subsumes FBI/CIA/NSA functions. No domestic surveillance authority. Violations: V+1 applied, publicly streamed.
items.explanation: Transparently chartered. Takes over FBI, CIA and NSA-type functions, with no domestic surveillance authority. Cell-citizens share the burden of staffing national security (the FBI, CIA and NSA functions). Workers have no special power to spy on citizens or profit from access. Discovered abuse means long, painful, publicly streamed death.

notes.quote: Cell-citizens will share the burden of maintaining and handling the national security elements for the body These groups do not have unique powers to spy on citizenry or use their information access to benefit etc. Discovery of such issues results in long painful and publicly streamed death.

items.label: Oversight body
items.desc: Elected separately. Dual function: internal accountability + diplomatic interface. Hard-scoped by design.
items.explanation: Separately elected, with two jobs: internal accountability and diplomatic interface. Tightly scoped. A small group elected separately by the cells. It acts as ambassadors and as local judges with prosecution authority over national-security workers, with scope kept narrow so it can build no leverage or military capability. With the national-security body it forms a two-part, self-correcting structure in place of three branches.

notes.quote: There actually should be a small dedicated group also separately elected by the cells to be the oversight for this group But they will have very limited scope to prevent building any possible level of leverage or militaristic capability that threatens the whole.

items.label: Immigration — tiered
items.desc: Foreign nationals: zero constitutional standing. Tiered entry (tourist/education/business = cell-permitted, short-term). Body floor + cell acceptance. Sharp penalties. No international body authority over borders.
items.explanation: Foreign nationals have no constitutional standing. Short-term entry (tourist, education, business) is cell-permitted. Body-floor citizenship requirements are universal. Sharp penalties for violations. No international authority over borders. First steps toward citizenship are body-wide. After the body requirements are met, the applicant must choose a cell and be accepted by a cell representative. The cell sets its own citizenship rules and names (e.g. Iron-Citizen, FreeFarming-Citizen). The path involves social or military service, learning the language and a longer period living in the chosen cell's culture.

notes.quote: Also, for the right to travel, this only applies to citizens. Foreign actors have zero constitutional backing. They will be strictly controlled in the country borders and the only path to citizenship is a grueling set of requirements that involve social/military service, learning the language, completing a longer amount of time in the culture of choice with a cell, but there will be sharp penalties for violations of immigration law. Just applying to and gaining the first steps is body-wide. The individual must select and be accepted by a representative of a cell. The cell defines all rules for citizenship for itself as a cell-citizen (likely the name like Iron-citizen or FreeFarming-citizen).

items.label: Resource contribution system
items.desc: Value-percentage based. 10-year review cycle. No default income tax.
items.explanation: Owner's example: a manufacturing-heavy cell's infrastructure sector with a 5% value share gives 5% of its steel beams to a body building for international trade. Contributions are product or profit percentages, agreed by all cells, adjustable as markets open or change, reviewed every 10 years. No default income tax.

notes.quote: Any items required for national level or external facing items for all cells will be funded by a clear dynamic value based system. This can be actual product, or profit percentages of product. As an example, the infrastructure sector in a cell that is manufacturing heavy could have a 5% value share that means giving 5% of its steel production for beams to build a federal building for international trade etc. These will be agreed upon by all cells and can be adjusted as new markets open or change every 10 years (long economic cycle).

items.label: Parity number system
items.desc: Technocratic, sector-owned, publicly transparent. All businesses require parity number at founding.
items.explanation: Technocratic, sector-owned, publicly transparent. Every business needs one at founding. Jointly set and controlled by the generators and owners of value. A new business works with authorities to develop its parity number. Values are dynamic and can change at any time. It is up to owners to enhance their number. The system is readily accessible.

notes.quote: The parity system has to be a technocratic item. It should be jointly set and controlled by the generators and owners of value. The system itself should be readily accessible. Even SaaS or other items can be given a parity number, in fact that will be a requirement for all items of work or industry or service etc. One core item for a new business is to work with authorities to develop a parity number that balances the value output based on a central understanding of transparent worth that is dynamic.

items.label: Progressive wealth equation
items.desc: Significant wealth permitted. Takeover-scale accumulation structurally prevented via ceiling.
items.explanation: A tag on the percentage of value generated, scaling to a clear degree regardless of cell. It allows doing very well but stops takeover-level wealth and untenable poverty.

notes.quote: Balance should be based on resource control primarily, and there can be basic anti monopoly rules set by cells for items like software or service etc. Wealth will not be prevented though. That will not prevent doing 'really' well but will stop takeover level wealth or levels of poverty that are untenable.

items.label: Birth accounts
items.desc: Body floor + cell additive. Funded from cell value percentages. No citizen starts at zero.
items.explanation: Body floor plus cell top-up, funded from cell value percentages. No citizen starts at zero.

notes.quote: Birth accounts come from value percentages in each cell. There is a smaller floor by body then a cell governed additive. There will also be a starting bank of sorts for all citizens at birth that can grow or be used for a variety of items and it's up to the citizen to handle it appropriately when of age

items.label: No mandatory welfare
items.desc: Voluntary support system + birth accounts replaces mandatory welfare.

notes.quote: That said there will be no mandatory social system like welfare, instead, a voluntary system will be setup and marketed by the body level for needs

items.explanation: None mandatory. Voluntary support plus birth accounts replace it.

items.label: Early adulthood petition
items.desc: 12+ with 75% judicial panel + mandatory parental inclusion. Rare genius cases can access agency early.
items.explanation: Age 12+ may petition. Hearing details are set by the cell. Parents are always part of the hearing. Passing needs a strict 75% agreement of the hearing group.

notes.quote: Btw one can petition at any age above 12 for adulthood based on a convening of judicial hearing details set by cell--but parents are always a part of it, and it is expected to be a strict 75% agreement of the hearing group. This allows genius level mature rare kids to secure power early enough to make an outsized difference while healthy and young.

items.label: Cell absorption rules
items.desc: Competitive incentive market. 90% dual supermajority (both cells). Accumulation ceiling enforced.
items.explanation: Struggling cells (below the floor threshold for a defined period) become eligible for absorption offers. Competing absorbers offer incentive packages (birth accounts, resource access, transfer perks, reduced contributions). Needs 90% in both cells (dual supermajority). The accumulation ceiling applies. No cell may exceed a set share of the total body resource base; approaching the ceiling ends eligibility to absorb, and the excess goes to new-cell formation or a struggling-cell recovery fund.

notes.quote: Absorption requires 90 percent of both affected cells to agree. A poor cell should still have a relative balance of resources. Whatever those are still matters to the body. Absorbing interests can offer incentives for initial absorption to drive a level of competition. That said, resource balancing still exists so a cell can't absorb all cells for control. There needs to be a rebalancing that incentivizes the absorber but limits overall accumulation.

items.label: Cell disbandment — prohibited
items.desc: Cells cannot be dissolved. Only absorbed with dual supermajority.

notes.quote: Disbandment is not allowed.

items.explanation: Prohibited. A cell can only be absorbed, never dissolved.

items.label: New cell formation process
items.desc: Body-wide formal process. Resource allocation review triggered on instantiation.
items.explanation: Body-wide formal process that triggers a resource allocation review. Founding geography: no cell holds the richest sources of several high-value resources (uranium, platinum, gold, tantalum) together. Where resources sit close together, cells are smaller.

notes.quote: New cells setup will follow formal processes involving all cells like in the beginning of resource allocation on instantiation of the country. There should be no cell that has the richest of all sources of say uranium, platinum, gold, tantalum all in one area.

items.label: WMD equal distribution
items.desc: Capability-defined (10,000+ casualties OR 1+ sq mile radius), technology-agnostic. Equal custody across cells. Cross-cell manning. No single-cell monopoly.
items.explanation: Defined by capability: 10,000+ casualties or 1+ square mile, regardless of technology. Equal custody across all cells; no single-cell monopoly. A body-wide clearance system with strict vetting draws equal numbers of participants across sectors. Where a function needs more people, representatives from other cells serve rotations or contracts, but headcount stays equal.

notes.quote: All weapons of mass destruction that become accessible...defined by some body metric like capable of 10000 or more death or more than a square mile of damage or something Will be equally shared between all cells out of mutual survival and need to balance the extreme nature. This means a body-wide clearance system with strict vetting that sources equal numbers of participants across sectors based on needed resources.

items.label: Inter-cell movement
items.desc: Citizen-preferenced process. Merit/achievement transfer pathway. Body citizenship portable.
items.explanation: Transfers follow a process like immigration, with preference to existing citizens. Accomplishments and awards can unlock transfer. Body citizenship is portable.

notes.quote: The new item is whether citizens of cells can move cells. This can be a process similar to immigration but preference given to citizens. Also perks could allow transfer due to accomplishment, award, etc.

items.label: Military posture
items.desc: No standing army. Universal service stays: a training and readiness term for all eligible men and women, disability-inclusive by role. Cell militias handle local events. Large-scale conflict is pre-committed by cell-to-body agreements with preordained cell specializations. Deployment beyond training is volunteers first; conscription only at grave trigger points (merit- and numbers-based, with perks, fixed rotations, escalating multi-cell override to extend). The national security body (c12) runs the outward-facing intelligence and development service, funded by cell contracts.
items.explanation: No standing army and no universal service. Cell militias handle local events. Large conflicts are pre-committed through cell-to-body agreements with preassigned cell specializations. Volunteers first; conscription only at grave trigger points, selected on merit and numbers, with perks, fixed rotations and an escalating multi-cell override to extend. The body may run an outward-facing intelligence and development service funded by cell contracts.

notes.quote: A mandatory service period of all eligible men and women with caveats for disability etc. Even physical disability will be utilized though. Training and upkeep will happen at all times, but given all citizens are potential troops, there is no need for a wasteful federal government backed standing army. Only external threats pull federal-like military action together.

items.label: Justice detail — cell jurisdiction
items.desc: Bail, jury and punishment detail are cell jurisdiction. Diverse cell justice systems are necessary, like biological cells. AI may assist jury and peer processes.
items.explanation: Bail, jury and punishment detail belong to the cells. Varied cell justice systems are intended, like cells in a body. AI may assist jury and peer processes.

notes.quote: The assumption is that cells will set bail and punishment rules, trial by what type of jury etc. to maintain a diverse and localized system that more closely reflects those close to the rules.

items.label: Emergency tax
items.desc: Flat, voted at cell or body level, hard-capped, hard-stopped. Sunset clauses are constitutional.
items.explanation: Flat, voted, hard-capped and hard-stopped. Sunset clauses are constitutional. Purpose: prevents infinite systems that justify their existence by never fixing streets or never cutting costs.

notes.quote: If needed, a tax can be levied, but it will be voted either at cell or body level and will always be a flat limited tax with clear rules and uniquely with hard stops. This prevents infinite systems that justify their existence with fraud or abuse by never fixing streets or never cutting costs etc.

items.label: Project-based funding entities
items.desc: Scoped, funded to their cohort's estimate, then refocused, disbanded or absorbed at completion.
items.explanation: Scoped to one project, funded to the estimate, disbanded or absorbed on completion. Owner's example: a body formed to beat a blight.

notes.quote: If a cell based government like entity is setup to tackle ...lets say a blight, they will be given the needed amounts estimated by their cohort to get scientists, international assistance, production of any chemical agents needed etc. And then when the blight is gone or finished, the group is either refocused, or disbanded and absorbed back into another role

items.label: Voluntary-service incentives
items.desc: Volunteering for internal problems earns benefits such as tax reduction or promotion weighting (owner's example: 10%).
items.explanation: Tax reduction and promotion weighting for those who serve voluntarily. Pairs with c26: volunteer deployment is what earns these.

notes.quote: Would likely require some level of benefit for their volunteering to assist an internal problem...like a 10% weight toward promotion or position or something...or maybe a reduction in taxes required for future efforts).

layers.label: Foundation
layers.description: Rights arbitration, NAP enforcement, hierarchy constraints. The enforcement substrate beneath the constitutional text.

items.label: 1A — Rights Arbitration Body
items.desc: Structure and glossary RESOLVED 2026-06-28. Option D augmented: both parties submit structured argument statements with judiciary-committee-scoped RAG factual records → AI parses statements + constitutional text → ruling recommendation → either party may reject → rotating panel, final, constitutional text only, no precedent accumulation. Glossary: immutable constitutional core. 1A-sub RESOLVED 2026-09-13 (hybrid of Options C and D — see Resolution Log). OPEN: arbiter qualification standards (now including body-level arbiter selection, moved from 5C), scope limits.

subitems.label: Structure selected — Option D augmented (statement + RAG + AI + panel)
Glossary — immutable constitutional core, annotation-only addenda
1A-sub: Judiciary committee — evidence-stage body, AI rubric by default, contest to a sortition committee drawn equally per cell
Qualification standards + selection for rotating panel arbiters (incl. body-level arbiter selection, moved from 5C)
Scope limits chartered (1A disputes vs. cell courts)
Evidentiary rubric — who writes and amends it

items.explanation: 1A-sub [RECALLED: 2026-09-13 memory log], clarified [DELEGATED 2026-10-04: agent pick under owner instruction, awaiting owner close]: the sortition committee and the rotating arbiter panel are two bodies at two stages. The committee rules on the factual record (evidence scope); the panel rules on the merits and is final. The committee is drawn equally per cell, matching Option A and the equal-per-cell pattern used for WMD manning and delegates. Residual: the rubric is now the capture point, so its authorship and amendment are open.

items.label: 1B — NAP Edge Cases
items.desc: Fraud, cross-cell environmental damage, psychological coercion, negligence. Each needs a constitutional answer or a defined arbitration pathway.

subitems.label: Fraud definition (takes without consent, no physical force — NAP violation?)
Negligence causing harm (unintentional — still NAP violation?)

items.label: 1C — Enforcement Hierarchy (absorbs 6B)
items.desc: Who enforces body-level constitutional violations if a cell refuses? Coordination body has no enforcement arm specified. Absorbed 6B (rogue cell enforcement) on 2026-09-13; its three sub-items are carried here.
items.explanation: Absorbed 6B on 2026-09-13 ([RECALLED: 2026-09-13 memory log]). 6B original text: "If a cell violates the body constitution and refuses compliance, what is the enforcement mechanism?" Option list from the founding conversation: economic sanctions by other cells, military action authorized by coordination-body supermajority, automatic resource reallocation, isolation with loss of representation and body-citizen protections until compliant.
items.description: What enforces body-level constitutional violations if a cell refuses compliance? The coordination body currently has no defined enforcement arm.

layers.label: Structure
layers.description: Cell model specifics, coordination body detail, minimum central functions. The skeletal architecture of the system.

items.label: 2A — Minimum Central Functions
items.desc: Enumerate what must exist at body level vs optional. Currency, standards body, courts, treaty functions.

notes.quote: So balance instead of a 3 part government here is based on a 2 part self-hosted self correcting national security structure.

items.description: What must exist at body level and what is optional: currency, standards body, courts, treaty functions.

items.label: 2B — Cell Internal Governance Floor
items.desc: Constitutional minimum for cell governance? Must be capable of producing a delegate. Can a cell be internally monarchic?
items.description: The constitutional minimum for a cell's internal government. It must be able to produce a delegate. Can a cell be internally monarchic?

items.label: 2C — Cell Size / Subdivision Trigger
items.desc: Population growth is uneven. When does a cell become too large? Subdivision trigger needed.

notes.quote: The cells can exist of their own interest or charter, but primarily they would be initially formed based on the technocratic federation idea to maximize resource handling. If resources are close then cells are smaller.

items.description: When a cell has grown too large, and what triggers a split.

items.label: 2D — Coordination Body Detail
items.desc: Delegate count, technocratic sectors, quorum, voting thresholds, term lengths, emergency sessions. Also owns: exact glossary amendment threshold (deferred from 1A).

subitems.label: Glossary amendment threshold (deferred from 1A — must exceed 3/4 + 75%)

notes.quote: This should be a hybrid that adjusts with population. If new cells are added or one is absorbed by 90% decree etc. then population can change the numbers. Otherwise, cells will elect delegates on a rotating basis from their governmental structure, but the core technocratic authorities (CEOs or corps etc) will have an equal represntation.

layers.label: Economic
layers.description: Capital, property, currency, technocratic federations. The economic substrate and its rules.

items.label: 3A — Currency Model
items.desc: Single body currency, cell currencies, or open competition? Monetary authority? Commodity/fiat/crypto-style?
items.description: One body currency, cell currencies, or open competition. Who is the monetary authority. Commodity, fiat, or crypto-style.

items.label: 3B — Property Rights
items.desc: Land ownership theory, intellectual property, commons/cross-cell resources, abandoned property reversion.

items.label: 3C — Cross-Cell Contracts
items.desc: Which cell's law governs cross-cell contracts? Who enforces? No interstate equivalent defined.
items.description: Which cell's law governs a contract between cells, and who enforces it.

items.label: 3D — Technocratic Federations
items.desc: What sectors exist at body level? Permanent or dynamic? Regulatory vs advisory authority? Cell economy interaction.

notes.quote: I'm also a fan of certain capitalistic or, let's say, federation state styles that maybe would help split items out more so you could have federation states as subgroups within the hierarchy that control certain aspects of, let's say, a certain industry, but not in a way that's tied to some central government, more a technocratic element.

items.description: Which sectors exist at body level; permanent or changing; regulatory or advisory power; how they interact with cell economies.

layers.label: Social
layers.description: Children, urban policy, family, cultural substrate. The human layer of the system.

items.label: 4A — Child Protection
items.desc: V+1 multiplier for crimes against children? Standing when parents are perpetrators? Body vs cell jurisdiction?

notes.quote: Then I would say children come next as they're a unique element that deserves an extra level of protection as well as, let's say, a censorship or a careful handling of their rights before they're able to properly understand and exercise them.

items.label: 4B — Education
items.desc: Body floor vs cell-defined? Private/market role? Civics/constitution curriculum required?

items.label: 4C — Urban Density
items.desc: Constitutional density ceiling per cell? Rural incentive structures? Parity weighting for rural production?

notes.quote: There is a clear problem with mental health, autonomy, and even just being generally nice to fellow humans that I don't see in many rural areas where people are forced to survive on their own So whatever can maximize spreading out these centers of power that create a hive mind of infantilized people who rely on a bunch of systems and generally lead to high taxes and eventually degradation, high crime, etcetera.

items.label: 4D — Family Definition
items.desc: Constitutional vs cell-defined? Legal rights of family unit vs individual? Divorce, inheritance, custody jurisdiction?

layers.label: Legitimacy
layers.description: AI role, law writing, judicial selection, transparency, accountability. How the system maintains integrity over time.

items.label: 5A — AI Governance
items.desc: Who owns/operates AI systems? Capture prevention? Audit mechanism? Conflict with elected body?

subitems.label: Audit mechanism — all outputs published; any cell may contest a pattern
AI vs elected body — human body prevails; AI output stands only uncontested
Phase-out fallback — 1A panel hears directly; sector owners maintain parity

items.explanation: Principle [RECALLED: 2026-09-13 memory log]: AI is always contestable and audited when contested; it is infrastructure, governance only where it fills bureaucratic holes and proves long-run utility; it can be phased out if too contestable. Picks [DELEGATED 2026-10-04: agent pick under owner instruction, awaiting owner close]: (1) every AI output is published, and any cell has standing to contest a pattern of outputs, not only a single case; this keeps 'audited when contested' and catches systematic bias. (2) In a conflict, the human body prevails; an AI output stands only while uncontested (axiom 8). (3) Phase-out fallback: 1A runs as its rotating panel directly, and parity numbers are maintained by the sector owners who already set them (c16).

notes.quote: I also think AI plays a role in the future for determining certain things, especially when you can now parse thousands of lines of laws and other elements and see where they contradict what makes sense, more understanding of data. And so I think that egalitarianism is going to become partly data driven.

items.label: 5B — Law Writing Process
items.desc: Cell law revision cycle? Body law revision process? Direct democracy, delegate-written, AI-drafted?
items.description: The revision cycle for cell law and for body law. Direct vote, delegate-written, or AI-drafted.

items.label: 5C — Judicial Selection
items.desc: Cell-level judges — elected, appointed, merit? Body-level arbiter selection moved to 1A (arbiter qualification standards) on 2026-09-13.
items.description: How cell-level judges are chosen: elected, appointed, or merit. Body-level arbiter selection moved to 1A. Whether c27 fully closes this item was not recorded.

items.label: 5D — Transparency Infrastructure
items.desc: Constitutional right to government data? Or cell-defined?
items.description: A constitutional right to government data, or cell-defined.

items.label: 5E — Corruption Standard
items.desc: Cell-level corruption handling. Body floor minimum for bribery, judicial capture, election fraud.
items.description: How cells handle corruption, and the body-level minimum for bribery, judicial capture and election fraud.

layers.label: Defense
layers.description: External threats, internal enforcement, police function, intelligence constraints. The security architecture.

items.label: 6A — Cross-Cell Command
items.desc: Who commands when external threat triggers body-level response? Sunset/return to cells post-threat?
items.description: Who commands when an external threat triggers a body-level response, and how command returns to the cells afterward. c26 sets who fights, not who commands.

items.label: 6C — Police Function
items.desc: Cell-controlled entirely? Constitutional floor for conduct? Who polices the police?

notes.quote: Almost all other items, even environmental or police corruption etc. are handled by cells.

items.label: 6D — Intelligence Constraints
items.desc: Cell surveillance authority? Voluntary intel sharing? Evidentiary standard? Foreign intel authorization?

items.label: 6E — Threat Definition
items.desc: What threshold triggers body-level military response? Authorization requirement to prevent abuse?
items.description: The threshold that triggers a body-level military response, and the authorization needed to prevent abuse. Partly blocks 6A.

axioms.name: Natural rights
axioms.text: Objective natural law exists. Rights are recognized, not granted. Defensible through deism, Christianity, or secular reason equally. Source-agnostic.

axioms.name: Soft determinism
axioms.text: Agency is real. Physics constrains but does not fully determine. Consciousness/soul have undetermined properties. Hard determinism rejected.

axioms.name: Hierarchy
axioms.text: Dominance hierarchy is a biological species-level fact, not a cultural artifact. Flat structures are unstable. Design must work with hierarchy, not against it.

axioms.name: NAP baseline
axioms.text: Non-Aggression Principle is the default behavioral norm. Voluntarism first. Coercion only where structurally necessary.

axioms.name: Subsidiarity
axioms.text: Power dispersed is power constrained. Decisions at the lowest competent level. Switzerland/canton model is the closest real-world approximation.

axioms.name: Anti-metropolitanism
axioms.text: Urban density pathologizes human behavior at scale. Rural interdependence produces better social outcomes. Design should structurally limit density concentration.

axioms.name: Children as protected class
axioms.text: Children hold rights in trust. NAP applies asymmetrically until capacity is established. Extra protection layer is constitutional, not discretionary.

axioms.name: AI as legitimacy tool
axioms.text: AI parses law for contradiction, maintains parity numbers, enables data-driven egalitarianism. It is infrastructure, not governance.

core_architecture.name: Cell Model
points: Cells = the canton analog. Named (e.g., "Iron-Cell," "FreeFarming-Cell").
Resource-balanced geography at founding — no cell holds monopoly on high-value natural resources.
Cells have their own constitutions, below the body constitution.
Cell-citizens hold dual identity: body-citizen status (portable) + cell-citizen status (cell-specific).
Cells compete for citizens — birth accounts, resources, quality of governance are differentiators.

core_architecture.name: WMD / National Security
points: WMD defined by capability metric (10k+ casualties or 1+ sq mile damage), technology-agnostic.
Equal distribution across cells — mutual assured balance, no cell achieves dominance.
Cross-cell equal contribution to manning — rotation/contract fills resource gaps, headcount stays proportional.
National security body: no domestic surveillance, transparently chartered.
Oversight body: separately elected, dual internal/external function, limited scope by design.
Violations of national security role: V+1 applied, publicly streamed — no permanent institutional capture possible.

core_architecture.name: Wealth / Economic Floor
points: Primary check: resource-balanced cell geography at founding.
Secondary check: body-level progressive contribution equation (scales with value, universal across cells).
Tertiary check: cell-level anti-monopoly rules for non-resource industries.
Parity number: all businesses/industries/services assigned dynamic transparent value metric by technocratic sector owners.
No mandatory welfare. Voluntary system + birth account = floor.
Struggling cell pathway: competitive absorption offers, 90% dual supermajority still applies, accumulation ceiling prevents dominant-cell rollup.

core_architecture.name: Citizenship
points: Body-level floor: universal minimum requirements, non-negotiable everywhere.
Cell-level acceptance: after body floor cleared, applicant selects and must be accepted by a specific cell.
Cell defines its own additional requirements above the body floor.
Entry vector problem solved: lenient cell can only grant cell-citizenship; body-citizenship requires clearing hard floor.

core_architecture.name: Coordination Body (framework — detail pending 2D)
points: Hybrid: rotating cell delegates + equal technocratic sector representation.
Population-adaptive scaling.
New cells or absorptions trigger rebalancing of representation numbers.

resolution_log.body:
Option D confirmed, then AUGMENTED by owner:
  - Both parties independently submit a structured statement of argument —
    a formal document pairing their legal/rights claim with a RAG-assembled
    factual record, filtered and scoped by a judiciary committee.
  - AI parses statements + constitutional text → ruling recommendation.
  - Either party may reject → escalates to rotating panel of human arbiters.
  - Panel ruling is final. Constitutional text only. No spirit-of-the-law.
    No precedent accumulation.
  Statement functions: (1) directs AI parsing from committee-vetted inputs,
  (2) routes factual disputes to trial instead of arbitration,
  (3) produces a higher-quality panel record on escalation.
  SECOND-ORDER: judiciary committee now exists as a required component
  → logged as 1A-sub (composition, selection, capture prevention).

Immutable constitutional core.
  - Philosophically derived at founding, cemented permanently.
  - Amendment threshold: astronomical — structurally ABOVE the standard
    additive process (3/4 + 75%). Exact threshold set at 2D.
  - Clarifications and factual addenda permitted as companion annotations
    ONLY — cannot alter the defined meaning of any core term.
  - No governing body may redefine a glossary term via any lighter process.

Hybrid of Options C and D (amended 2026-09-13):
  - AI applies a published evidentiary rubric by default.
  - Either party may contest and escalate, with counsel, to a
    sortition-drawn committee bound by the same rubric.
  - The rotating arbiter panel audits only when a decision is contested,
    never by random sample.

Rogue cell enforcement (6B) merged into 1C.
  Owner principle: merge what can be merged; simplicity and non-redundancy
  are primary goals of the whole system.
  6B original text (preserved, not deleted):
    "If a cell violates the body constitution and refuses compliance, what
    is the enforcement mechanism?"
    Sub-items: economic sanctions mechanism · military authorization
    threshold · isolation / representation loss.
  The three sub-items now sit under 1C. 6B no longer appears as a node.

Body-level arbiter selection moved out of 5C into 1A (arbiter qualification
  standards + selection). 5C keeps cell-level judge selection.
  Original 5C sub-item (preserved): "Body-level arbiter selection".

- Always contestable; audited only when contested.
  - AI is infrastructure. It is governance only where it fills bureaucratic
    holes and proves long-run utility.
  - Can be phased out if it proves too contestable.
  Recorded as a principle. 5A sub-items (ownership, capture prevention,
  audit, AI vs elected body) stay not-started until the owner says whether
  this principle closes any of them.

working_principles: The eight axioms are fixed starting points. Every decision must trace back to them, and none is open for debate.
The constitutional layer is additive only. Nothing is ever removed from it.
Resolved items are not reopened without an explicit instruction from the owner.
Any loose end a decision creates is logged and queued, never silently dropped.
Merge what can be merged. Simplicity and non-redundancy are primary goals of the whole system (2026-09-13).

AI is always contestable and is audited only when contested. It takes on a governing role only where it fills a bureaucratic hole and proves long-run usefulness, and it can be phased out if it draws too many challenges (2026-09-13).
